speaker: Doctor
text: Since your CBC and electrolyte results are pending, let's focus on the progression of your weakness: does the difficulty climbing stairs get worse when you stand up from a chair, and have you noticed any trouble speaking or swallowing?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of bulbar symptoms (swallowing/speech) and respiratory issues, combined with a one-month gradual onset, makes a rapidly progressive crisis less likely. Given your upper limb weakness alongside diplopia, could you describe if your double vision worsens when you look up or down, and do you experience any tingling or numbness in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of weakness worsening with exertion and improving with rest is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder; has your double vision fluctuated significantly during the day or after prolonged reading? REQUEST IMAGES: EMG (Electromyography) and Nerve_Conduction_Study.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating diplopia and proximal weakness that worsens with exertion (fatigability) but improves with rest is the classic presentation of this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder, and the absence of bulbar or respiratory symptoms further supports this diagnosis over other mimics.
